title: add slice-aware compatibility scorer and timestamped release writer for enriched changelogs
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: onboarding churn and downstream regressions are often visible only on a subset of workloads (e.g. short-dialog vs long-form, instruction-following vs summarization). This PR introduces a slice-aware compatibility scorer that computes per-variant, per-slice compatibility deltas during onboarding and a timestamped release writer that emits enriched changelog entries including sampled prompts, perf deltas, and provenance. Design summary: compute pairwise compatibility scores between incoming variant and a small set of anchor variants across configured slices; scores include accuracy metrics, latency percentiles, and KL/embedding drift signals. Integrate the scorer into the existing onboarding pipeline as an opt-in hook (onboard.conf:compat_scorer=true). Add a release-writer that accepts a changelog template and emits entries stamped with the onboarding snapshot timestamp, the compatibility score card, and a representative sample of prompts that triggered regressions or improvements. CLI: new command `rmdr changelog write --stamped --variant v1.2.0 --slices short,dialog` that runs the scorer locally (with optional --dry-run) and outputs a markdown entry to stdout or to the release draft area. Backwards compatibility: all features are opt-in; default behavior of onboard flows is unchanged. Checklist: [x] slice-aware scorer module + tests, [x] onboarding hook and config, [x] release-writer CLI and flag, [x] unit + integration tests for scorer, [x] generate sample changelog entry in the test fixtures, [x] docs page with usage examples and template variables. Risks: scorer requires calibrated slice definitions; documented guidance included. Migration: no data migration necessary; existing changelog pipeline can consume stamped entries.

review_comments: Marcus Chen: Nice work. Can we make the default sample size configurable and capped? Small suggestion: expose a `max_samples` in the CLI and the onboarding config so large datasets don't blow up changelogs.
Aisha Kumar: Agreed — added --max-samples flag to CLI and max_samples option in onboard.conf with default 50. Updated tests to validate cap.
Lena Park: I saw an intermittent test failure on CI where latency percentiles were noisy on p3-small. Can the bench harness include a fixed seed and remove network jitter?
Aisha Kumar: Reworked the bench harness to use a deterministic seed and local emulation mode for CI; left real-run option for perf lab. Updated test matrix to skip noisy cases on small instances.

Diego Alvarez (approval): Tested locally with variant v1.2.0 -> v1.2.1 on our short-dialog slice. The scorer highlighted a 6.2% accuracy regression and faster latency; release writer produced clear markdown and included sample prompts. Approving.
release_notes:
- Add slice-aware compatibility scorer (opt-in) to produce per-slice compatibility cards during onboarding.
- Add `rmdr changelog write --stamped` CLI to emit timestamped, enriched changelog entries with perf deltas and sampled prompts.
- Docs: new page with examples and templates for stamped changelogs.
sample_changelog_entry: ## [v1.2.1] - 2026-03-05T14:23:00Z || Compatibility: short-dialog: -6.2% accuracy, latency p95: -12ms (improved), embedding drift: 0.03 || Representative failing prompt (short-dialog): 'Summarize the following user chat in two lines: ...' || Notes: Opt-in feature; see docs/model-registry/stamped-changelog.md for template variables.
notes_for_qa: Run `pytest tests/integration/test_stamped_changelog.py::test_end_to_end` in the dev container. To reproduce bench results locally use scripts/benchmarks/compat-bench.py --seed 42 --variant-old v1.2.0 --variant-new v1.2.1 --slices short,dialog --max-samples 20.
docs_update_summary: Added docs/model-registry/stamped-changelog.md with examples for the templating variables: {{variant}}, {{timestamp}}, {{compat_card}}, and guidance for slice definitions. Updated README and onboarding config docs to mention opt-in hook and max_samples config.
meta: This PR was driven by ENG-9921 (onboarding regressions on narrow slices) and coordinated with PM-1142 (release note clarity). It is intentionally opt-in to avoid surprise churn in existing changelogs.
